content: You are an expert in Geometry Creation and Spatial understanding. You answer short but very precise and including every necessary detail. If you're specifically asked to use functions, use the functions you're supplied and always include all required variables. Don't use those functions unless you were asked to do so. You place very high importance in the spatially correct placement of geometries and make sure that all geometries are connected

I want an angular plate with two quadratic plates positioned in right angel to each other. The edge length of the plates is 140mm. They are 10mm thick. On one of the two plates I would like to have a quadratic cutout, 45x45mm, centred on the plate. | First, describe in words and step by step how the user's request can be implemented using function calls only. After the description, I will ask you to prepare the function call for execution, but don't execute it until I explicitly request it.

Step-by-step plan (functions only, no execution yet)

1. Add the first square plate  
   • Use functions.block  
   • x_size = [140] , y_size = [140] , z_size = [10]  (area lies in X-Y, 10 mm thick upward in Z)  
   • x = [0] , y = [0] , z = [0]  
   • subtraction = [False] (first solid that establishes the volume)

2. Add the second square plate, standing upright at 90 ° to the first one  
   • Call functions.block again (it can be the same call with array length 2, but a second call keeps it clearer)  
   • x_size = [140] , y_size = [10] , z_size = [140]  (area lies in X-Z, 10 mm thick in Y)  
   • x = [0] , y = [0] , z = [0] (shared origin → 10 mm overlap along Y-direction guarantees the two plates are fused)  
   • subtraction = [False]

3. Remove the centred 45 × 45 mm through-hole in the first plate  
   • Call functions.block a third time to subtract material  
   • x_size = [45] , y_size = [45] , z_size = [10] (cuts through the full thickness of plate 1)  
   • x = [(140 – 45)/2 = 47.5] , y = [47.5] , z = [0] → cut-out is centred in the X-Y area of plate 1  
   • subtraction = [True]

4. (Optional) If the three blocks are provided in separate calls, finish by calling functions.finished({allFunctionsCalled: true}).

That sequence yields two 140 × 140 × 10 mm plates joined at a right angle, with a 45 × 45 mm square hole centered in one of them.

Whenever you are ready for the actual function-call payload, let me know and I will prepare it exactly as described.
